problems.issue: root fairing: structurally the cap is neutral, and the 25.8 -> 24.2 MPa hub_fea drop is not a strength gain. I compared the cached FEA fields. The baseline mesh had 13.8k elements and the new one has 16.7k. The cap adds about 2400 lightly loaded elements (95th percentile 3 MPa), which pulls the 99.9th percentile down without lowering any real stress. Over the same change the volume peak went from 64 to 83 MPa and the deflection from 7.8 to 8.2 mm, which is mesh refinement. problems.issue: root fairing: print and mass. (a) As printed (boss on the bed, airfoil floating above it on tree supports, 30.9 % of the surface supported), the lower half of the half-ellipse nose faces down and sits on supports. The folded-mode leading edge will carry support scars on exactly the surface Spencer asked to be faired. (b) The 0.3 mm lip is thinner than one 0.42 mm line, so the slicer drops it or leaves a blob. That is harmless, but the shape that prints is not the modelled one. (c) The cap is an 18.2 cm3 solid loft per hub (hub 194.6 cm3). At 4 walls and 40 % infill that is roughly 8 g per hub
problems.fix: Add a height-range or part modifier giving the cap 10-15 % infill (walls unchanged). Tell the builder to sand the nose's lower half smooth after removing supports (ASSEMBLY note), or set support interface layers and a Z gap that leave a better finish there. Fade the lip either to >= 0.45 mm or to zero, e.g. end the loft on a degenerate section by intersecting with a fading wedge.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: root fairing: what still faces the flow after the change. I re-measured the designer's own metric (planar B-rep faces within 30 deg of square to the relative wind). It is 11 mm2 at 0 deg, 0 mm2 at 35 deg and 51 mm2 at 70 deg, so the 2803 -> 51 mm2 claim reproduces. The nose has the same YZ section at every sweep angle, which is the right section by simple sweep theory (the flow mostly runs root-to-tip when folded). That answers the ask at 0, 35 and 70 deg. The planar metric does not catch two leftovers. (1) Folded at 70 deg, the V keel's inboard 45 deg face (x 130-205, y 26.3-36, down to z -9.
problems.fix: For x 130..176, extend the cap's half-ellipse down to the keel's depth (the nose wraps the keel), so the keel's inboard face becomes the lower half of the nose. It stays 0.6 mm above the cover as the keel does now. This also adds section depth exactly where hub_fea fails, so the aero fix and the strength fix point the same way.

problems.issue: hub_fea fails: p99.9 von Mises 24.2 MPa against 17.5 allowed (CF-PETG / SF 2), and 8.2 mm deflection at the root leading edge (14.7, 90) against a 1.0 mm limit, 8 times over. The load arrives where it should (32 N lift split across the spar sockets, 6.2 / -3.0 / 1.5 N m), and the plot's hot spot is where the load path says it should be: the thin root trailing edge between the rear spar and the boss. The architecture sends the whole half-wing's lift moment through the last 25 mm of the root airfoil (about 2-5 mm thick even with the keel and collar) into a 20 mm boss that is held only at its pin
problems.fix: Make the section from the rear spar socket to the boss a full-depth box: merge the keel, collar and root cap into one deep web, at least 15-20 mm deep, running into the boss. Grow the boss (r 10 -> 13) and the collar. Move the lead channel off the root-face ligament (see the fairing minor). Run the rear spar socket as close to the boss as the sector allows. If the deflection is still over 1 mm, bo

problems.issue: hub_l is the mirror image of hub_r: same section, same 6 g load, same thin root trailing edge into a 20 mm boss. It has no FEA of its own, so the hub_r hub_fea failure (24.2 vs 17.5 MPa, 8.2 vs 1.0 mm) applies to it unchanged.
problems.fix: Fixed by the same hub.py change as hub_r (both are built from right_body). Re-run hub_fea after the fix. Optionally add a hub_l FEA case so the failure table stops showing hub_l as 'no strength case'.

problems.issue: spine_fea fails: 53.6 MPa against 16 allowed (3.4 times over), and 2.1 mm deflection against 0.5. Each pin is in single shear at the arm: the load enters 33 mm along the pin, which adds a 5016 N mm moment at the bore. The arm is a 6 mm PETG plate hanging off the ridge, and its two root corners are declared sharp in the hottest zone (spine [200, +-14, 13.5], utilisation about 4.0). The wing's whole bearing couple goes through this plate, so the upper pivot would yield in the first hard pull-out.
problems.fix: Re-section the arm: 10-12 mm deep with a real fillet or gusset down to the ridge (reshape the boss top or the collar so the fillet has room). Or put the pin in double shear, or use an aluminium or CF top plate pressed onto the pin. Re-run spine_fea at the same load.

problems.issue: deck_fea did not run ('PLC Error: A segment and a facet intersect'), so the lower pivot plate (deck) has no strength proof. It carries the same pin bearing couple that overloads the spine arm 3.4 times. The failure table lists aft_fuse at '0 %', which really means 'unknown'.
problems.fix: Clean up the deck and stop-post geometry so it meshes. It is probably the same sliver and sharp-corner geometry as the 103 undeclared corners below. Then run deck_fea and size the deck and ribs from the result.

problems.issue: 103 sharp inside corners (1281 mm of edge) are neither filleted nor declared, e.g. [226.4, 0, -15.5], [221, 0, -12.5], [218, +-26.2, -72.3], plus 8 that fillet_inside reported it could not do near (222, +-27.5..+-12, -24.5) and (210.7, +-8.7, -13). Several are on the deck, the keel rib and the rear lug, all in the pin load path.
problems.fix: Fix the corners that failed to fillet (adjust plate edges so a 1.5 mm cove fits) or declare each with its reason. In particular, fillet the deck-to-rib and rib-to-lug junctions.

problems.issue: The aileron servo leads are too short: ail_r_pwr/sig and ail_l_pwr/sig are declared at 620 mm, but the routed path at full fold plus 15 % slack is 719.9 / 727.5 mm. As declared, the aileron servos cannot reach the flight controller.
problems.fix: Declare about 750 mm leads, or a 150-200 mm extension per servo (with a catalog entry and its source), and put the extension in the BOM and WIRING.md.

problems.issue: About 45 wiring routes pass through solid parts instead of holes or channels. The main lead and the phase wires go through fwd_fuse, motor_mount and the battery. The servo, GPS and tail leads go through fwd_fuse, aft_fuse, spine, hatch, tail_mount and hub_r. The aileron leads go through wing_r1/r2 and wing_l1/l2 (127-137 mm3 each), even though the wings have a 4 mm lead channel, so the declared route does not follow it. WIRING.md cannot be built as written.
problems.fix: Route every run through the features that exist: the wing and hub lead channel, the bulkhead pass-through, the spine GPS hole. Where none exists, add a hole or channel in the part that owns the wall. Then re-check until there are 0 'runs through' problems.

problems.issue: Aerodynamics at full spread: the ridge's front is a vertical face about 28 mm wide and 17 mm tall, chamfered only on its top edge. It sits square to the flow in the 32 mm channel the two new root caps now form ahead of x 100.
problems.fix: Give the ridge front a wedge or ogive nose in plan view (tapering from |y| 14 to ~4 over ~25 mm), not just a top chamfer. Keep the GPS pad and the front bolts (x 108) inside it.

problems.issue: Overbuilt parts in a mass-limited aircraft. fwd_fuse is 183.5 g of PLA working at 6 % of allowable with 100 % of its volume cold, tail_mount is at 3 % and motor_mount at 4 %. AUW is 1591 of 1650 g, wing loading 87.7 of 95 g/dm2 and stall speed 41.5 of 45 km/h, so every gram matters.
problems.fix: Leave the wall count alone: ENGINEERING.md s5 keeps 4 perimeters on parts with a strength check. Remove idle material instead. Add lightening windows in the battery-bay side walls (outside the hatch ledges, kept clear of the strap slots), shorten or open the shelf where nothing sits, and lower the infill on fwd_fuse and tail_mount at the reported cold zones. Then re-run fuse_fea and tail_fea.

problems.issue: The 4 M3 horn-screw holes leave only 71 % of the ring material near the tooth roots (pinion_l the same). Lewis bending already runs at 13.6 of 16 MPa (85 %).
problems.fix: Print at 100 % infill (already set) and check that the screw circle can move 0.5 mm inward on the horn pattern (catalog). If not, make the pinion 2 mm wider (the face width helps Lewis directly).

problems.issue: The 4 sweep-servo screws on each side need a ball-end 2.5 mm key (a straight key hits the servo body), and the sweep_servo insert holes sit at 88 % edge material.
problems.fix: Put 'ball-end 2.5 mm key' in the ASSEMBLY tools list, or move the servo tab shelf so a straight key reaches.

problems.issue: Thin walls below 1.2 mm: elevator 0.93, rudder 0.86, ail_r/l 1.02-1.03, hatch 1.01, tail_mount 1.12 mm.

problems.issue: Pre-existing print setup: the hub is printed boss-down, so the whole airfoil block floats about 15 mm above the bed on tree supports (30.9 % of the surface). That gives a poor lower surface on the most stressed and most aerodynamically exposed printed part.
problems.fix: Keep the orientation (the boss and gear need it), but add support interface layers and a 0.2 mm top Z distance for CF-PETG, and an ASSEMBLY note to sand the lower surface and the root nose.

problems.issue: Root fairing (this change): nothing guards the new over-travel clearance. The nose-to-ridge gap (0.451 mm at -3 deg) is now right, but no requirement checks it. clearance_min only samples inside the joint range [0, 70], and hard_stop only compares aft_fuse with the hub. If anyone changes RIDGE_HW, CAP_MAX, STOP_GAP or pivot_x later, it can touch again before the stop and every check will still pass. STATUS.md records this as an open engine gap, which is honest, but it is still open. Note: a hub-vs-spine clearance check would read 0.0 mm today because of the spine fillet / boss rub (separate ma
problems.fix: Engine: give clearance_min a 'beyond' pose (or have hard_stop report any third part that touches the moving part before the stop pair does), with a test. Then add hub_r-spine and hub_l-spine clearance requirements >= 0.3 mm at fold -3 deg (and >= 0.5 mm over 0..70).

problems.issue: Root fairing (this change): the nose has a wave in plan view (top render). I measured its reach inboard of the root face: 10.0 mm at x 35-65, down to 6.3 at x 100, back up to 7.7 at x 135, then fading to zero by x 165. The dip is the ridge limit at the ridge front. Aft of that the limit relaxes, because a point closer to the pin swings less, so the reach grows again. The rule is physically correct, but the result is a hump with no purpose on the folded leading edge, and it reads as unintended. This is cosmetic and slightly aerodynamic, not a clearance problem.
problems.fix: Use the running minimum of the ridge limit from x 95 aft (each station takes the smallest limit at or ahead of it). The reach then falls smoothly from 10 to about 6.3 mm and stays level until the fade starts at x 150. hub_l follows (built from the same body).

problems.issue: Infill (pre-existing geometry; the engine check is new, kerf/infill.py). hub_r prints at 15 % infill, so its core is a lattice about 2 % as strong as solid plastic. The FEA puts stress up to 22.7 times that deeper than the 1.68 mm walls, over 34 % of the part's volume, worst near (188.4, 35.5, -5.7): 13.8 MPa mean and 20.3 MPa max within 4 mm. ENGINEERING.md 3b says that stress must stay under the lattice strength. It also means the failing hub_fea numbers are optimistic: they assume a solid core. hub_l is identical.
problems.fix: Add a 100 % infill modifier box over the root block and boss (about x 140-215, y 16-45, full height, including the sector web), or raise the whole hub to >= 60 % infill with more wall loops. Keep the outboard root airfoil and the nose at 15 %. Put it in PRINT_SETTINGS / the 3MF, re-run the build and confirm the infill warning is gone.

problems.issue: Zero running clearance to each hub boss (pre-existing geometry, found now; this change did not cause it). spine.py runs fillet_inside (r 2) after cutting the r 11 boss holes. The ridge-to-cover cove therefore runs the full ridge length (x 100.3-220.7) out to y +-16 at z -10, and over each boss hole it leaves a 0 to 0.27 mm sliver (6.2 mm2, x 195.4-204.6). The hub boss (r 10 about the pin at y +-26) is tangent to that cove at (200, +-16, -10). I measured exactly 0.000 mm at fold 0, -1.4 and -3 deg, and it is the same at every fold angle because the boss turns about its own axis. ENGINEERING.md
problems.fix: In spine.py, exempt the cove inside the boss hole footprint (the keep callback, or cut the boss and lead holes after fillet_inside), so the hole rim stays at r 11, 1 mm off the boss. Add clearance_min hub_r-spine and hub_l-spine >= 0.5 mm over fold_r / fold_l 0..70 so it stays fixed.

problems.issue: Infill (pre-existing geometry; the engine check is new). The spine prints at 15 % infill, and the FEA puts stress up to 39.2 times the lattice strength deeper than the walls, over 17 % of its volume, worst near (203.3, 23.3, 15.2): the arm and ridge round the pin. ENGINEERING.md 3b. The failing spine_fea (solid assumption) is therefore optimistic too.
problems.fix: Add a 100 % infill modifier over both arms and the ridge from x 185 to 220 (or print the spine at 100 %, it is 60 g), as part of the arm re-section.
